info.title: Game Narrator API
info.summary: The /api/v1 surface of the Game Narrator appliance.
info.description: Hand-written and contract-tested. internal/api/openapi_contract_test.go fails when a route is registered without being documented here, when an operation's x-required-role disagrees with the auth scope table, or when a handler's success body stops validating against the schema below (docs/spec/08, ADR-0017). Errors are RFC 9457 problem+json documents carrying the stable code member of docs/spec/08's error contract plus the X-Request-Id correlation header. Reads of a profile revision carry an ETag equal to its quoted row_version; the writes that change one require it back as If-Match (412 on mismatch, 428 when absent). x-required-role is the minimum role the scope table grants an operation; public means no credential is needed. The table itself is auth.DefaultPolicy, explained in docs/adr/0016-authentication-and-sessions.md.

get.summary: Process liveness; no dependency probing.
Dependency readiness; a failing dependency answers 503.
get.description: checks is always an object: a dependency appears only once something has probed it, so an empty map honestly means nothing is wired rather than everything works (docs/spec/13). The database check's integrity verdict is cached, not re-run per request (ADR-0097): the full PRAGMA integrity_check runs at startup and on a schedule, and the answer reports the verdict's age in integrity_age_seconds so a stale ok is visible; a failing verdict keeps the fixed error string (no host paths).

503.description: Not ready — the same body, so a load balancer sees one shape for both outcomes and `checks` names what failed. A failure of the endpoint itself (a wrong method, an unwired route) is the problem+json default like anywhere else.

get.summary: Build, Go and machine capacity. Never paths, hostnames or secrets.
One snapshot of what the box is doing, with the canonical status string.
get.description: The global status bar's read (docs/design/plum-peach Global chrome): the active session (game, mode, capture fps actual vs target, dropped frames, the frame-to-voice p50 the session samples per line, lines spoken), the active onboarding runs (state, stage, characters voiced vs total, elapsed), the health rollup from cached probes only (a component nobody has probed is unknown, never a fresh probe), and the device (version, uptime, bound listen address). status is the server-rendered short string every client shows (RenderStatus): a fresh assembly per request, so a polling viewer gets the same number the push side publishes.

get.summary: The status snapshot's on-change push: SSE of status.changed frames with Last-Event-ID resume.
get.description: The bar's push half. Every frame carries id: <global seq> and the full snapshot as its data (the same shape GET /api/v1/status answers), so a reconnect with Last-Event-ID replays the missed frames from the hub's bounded log and a cursor older than the log gets the resync-required notice, the same machinery the event stream documents (docs/spec/08 Event stream reliability). The push side is one process-wide engine that assembles at 2 Hz and publishes only when the displayed shape changed, coalesced to at most one frame per 500 ms. The stream carries no gameplay text: counters, a status string and health levels, which is what keeps it at the viewer tier of the developer-tier event stream it rides on.

parameters.name: last_event_id
parameters.description: Query-string form of the Last-Event-ID header, for clients that cannot set headers.

get.summary: The ⌘K command-palette search: games, characters, lines, traces, settings sections and actions in one grouped response.
get.description: One debounced call behind the UX-02 overlay (ADR-0098, docs/design/plum-peach). The query is normalised (trimmed, internal whitespace collapsed) and echoed as agent_prompt: the string the overlay's Tab key hands to the agent dock. Groups appear in the fixed order game, character, line, trace, setting, action; an empty group is omitted, and an empty query is the palette's recents mode rather than an error. Scores are higher-is-better within a group: name fields and the static registries rank the match class (exact 3, prefix 2, contains 1) plus a recency boost of at most 1.0, lines rank the trigram index's bm25 negated to the higher-is-better direction plus the same boost, and because the boost stays below the 1.0 class gap, recency can reorder within a match class, never across one. The route is viewer; the body narrows per result: trace rows exist only for a developer-or-above caller, a settings section only for a role that may open the page it links to, and each action verb only for the role it names. Row targets follow the plum-peach IA (ADR-0093): the library focuses a game, cast lives at /games/:id/cast, traces at /traces and health at /health.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: The palette query. Absent or whitespace-only is the recents mode: each requested kind answers with its most recent items.

parameters.name: kinds
parameters.description: A comma-separated subset of game, character, line, trace, setting and action; defaults to all of them. An unknown kind is a 400: a silently-ignored kind would be a client bug the response could not show.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The per-kind ceiling: the palette shows at most one screen of any one kind, so the bound is tighter than a full search page's.

200.description: The grouped results, in the palette's canonical kind order.

get.summary: The host vitals: CPU, RAM, storage and thermal state (public).
get.description: A system-info-class read (docs/spec/08): host capacity and state, no game content, no host paths beyond the data directory's base name, no secrets. Public because the /diagnostics page must work before an account exists; every unmeasurable part answers null with the fact stated (no thermal zones exposed is unknown, not cool).

get.summary: The recent system logs, redacted (developer).
get.description: The newest records of the process's bounded log ring, every value passed the support-bundle redactor (URLs, tokens, private IPs). Developer tier like the dev-trace evidence route: system logs can carry provider request detail (docs/spec/14). ?limit= defaults to 200, capped 1000; a bad limit is 400, an unwired ring is 503.

post.summary: Start a diagnostics run: the host snapshot plus the doctor's probe of the named roles (operator).
post.description: Answers 202 with the run id and executes out-of-band — a role probe's budget is minutes, and a request that holds that long is a wedged connection. Each named role runs the doctor's own providers.<role> check (ADR-0087: the CLI's probe, never a copy): the content probe, the model-list check and the measured answer latency. Zero roles asks for the host snapshot only; a name that is not one of docs/spec/06's seven is a 400.

get.summary: One diagnostics run's current shape (viewer).
get.description: A running run reports the host snapshot and the role rows answered so far; a done run adds finished_at. 404 for an id that was never created or already fell out of the bounded store (the 32-newest, one-hour-TTL bound — a probe nobody polls is not appliance state).

get.summary: The multiplexed SSE stream, with Last-Event-ID replay.
get.description: Every frame carries id: <global seq>. A cursor older than the durable log's window is answered with events.resync_required before live frames. Decision-family payloads only reach a developer-or-above stream (docs/spec/08: partial data redacted when not in developer mode).

parameters.name: last_event_id
parameters.description: Query-string form of the Last-Event-ID header, for clients that cannot set headers.

get.summary: Whether the appliance is still unclaimed.

post.summary: Claim the appliance by creating the first admin (loopback only).

201.description: The admin exists; no session was minted.

post.summary: Exchange credentials for a session cookie and a CSRF token.
Revoke the calling session.

get.summary: Who the caller is, and the CSRF token for its session.

post.summary: Change the caller's password; revokes every session and token of the account.

get.summary: Every account. Never a hash.

post.summary: Create an account with a role no higher than the caller's.
Withdraw an account, revoking its sessions and tokens in the same transaction.
Restore an account. Revocations are not undone.
Admin password reset; revokes the account's sessions and tokens.

get.summary: An account's API tokens, by label. Never the secret.

post.summary: Mint an API token. The secret appears once, in this response.
Revoke one API token permanently.

get.summary: The title library, cursor-paginated.
get.description: Ordering is by ULID id, which is what makes a page boundary a row identity rather than an offset a concurrent import could shift (docs/spec/12's no-duplicates-or-gaps property). Text search is per revision (GET /api/v1/profiles/{id}/messages/search), because a match is only meaningful against one edition's script; ?q= here is refused rather than answered with an unfiltered list, which would read as “no title matches”.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Not supported on this collection: any value answers 501 NOT_SUPPORTED.

post.summary: Add a title family.
post.description: Requires an Idempotency-Key. The same key with the same body replays the original 201 with Idempotency-Replayed: true; the same key with a different body is a 422. A duplicate slug is a separate fact and answers 409: a collision to resolve, not a retry to absorb (ADR-0017).

get.summary: One title family, by ULID id or by slug.

patch.summary: Correct a title family's metadata in place.
patch.description: Games and editions carry no row version: docs/spec/08 puts ETag/If-Match on profile revisions, and internal/store/repo_catalog.go explains why a lost title edit is a nuisance while a lost dialogue edit is corruption. An omitted field is left alone and an empty object is a no-op that answers 200 with the unchanged row.

get.summary: Every edition (region x language x disc revision) of one title.

post.summary: Bind a game to a region, language and disc revision.
post.description: editions_identity_idx makes (game, region, language, revision) unique, so re-declaring the same disc is a 409 rather than a second row.

source_identity.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the exact image this edition was observed against.

get.summary: Every revision of one edition, lowest first.
get.description: Deliberately unpaginated: the row count grows once per human publish click (internal/store/repo_profiles.go argues it).

post.summary: Start a new draft lineage for one edition.
post.description: Takes no body: the revision number is server-owned, and a field that looks like one is refused rather than ignored.

post.summary: Re-import a .gnprofile.json as a brand-new draft of this edition.
post.description: Never an overwrite: ids are minted again and every internal reference is remapped, because a re-import that could target a published revision would be a way to edit what sessions are narrating (ADR-0015). sources_needing_bytes names the source hashes this appliance does not hold, i.e. what must be re-attached before the revision can be re-parsed or audited.

parameters.name: force
parameters.description: Accept a language or region mismatch against the target edition. For the deliberate case only.

voices_written.description: Approved voice rows written from the manifest voices section (ADR-0101).

voices_skipped.description: Voices already held under the same id and fingerprint (a re-import).

voice_refs_missing.description: Reference blobs the manifest named that this appliance does not hold; the pointer travels, the bytes travel only inside a .gnpack. These voices are not written.

voices_conflicts.description: Voices whose (character, revision) slot another voice already holds; reported, not written.

get.summary: The one revision this edition serves to sessions.
get.description: 404 when nothing is published: a session that cannot name a revision must refuse to start rather than choose one (docs/spec/13).

get.summary: One revision, with its concurrency token.

200.description: The revision. ETag is its quoted row_version; the writes below require it back as If-Match.

delete.summary: Soft-delete a revision: the mark with its retention window (FR-02).
delete.description: deleted_at + purge_after (72h) land in one compare-and-swap (ADR-0107). The 200 body is the marked profile, the receipt. Refusals: publication history (0004: the audit trail outlives the revision), derived revisions, an active session pinned to the profile (PROFILE_IN_USE), or an already-deleted mark. The row stays on disk until the purge.

200.description: The marked profile (the receipt): deleted_at and purge_after filled in.

post.summary: Derive a new draft from this revision: the only way to edit shipped content.
post.description: No If-Match: the parent may be immutable, which is exactly the case this call exists for, and a snapshot cannot corrupt the row it read.

post.summary: Move a revision along draft to review (and back), or retire a published one.
post.description: to=published is refused with 409: publication is the validated, digested, pointer-swapped, audited act, not a column write. The reachable targets are in the revision's own next_states.

200.description: Moved. ETag is the new row_version.

post.summary: Set the profile's narrator fallback (ADR-0101).
post.description: Decides whether a line whose speaker has no approved voice is spoken by the narrator voice. On by default (the profile row's DEFAULT 1) and the historical runtime behaviour; a line the setting holds back is skipped with reason narrator_fallback_disabled, and a line even the narrator could not speak is no_approved_voice.

200.description: The dial is set. ETag is the profile's row_version (the write does not bump it, but the token still answers against the revision you last read).

post.summary: Ship a review-ready revision, atomically archiving its predecessor.
post.description: The publish gate runs first and lists every finding. A refusal is 422 with code CONTENT_RIGHTS_REVIEW_REQUIRED when the finding is the rights gate and VALIDATION_FAILED otherwise, and problems names every issue either way (docs/spec/03's review screen).

get.summary: The publication history of this revision's edition, newest first.
One page of a revision's dialogue.
get.description: profile_etag is the revision's current If-Match token, so the dialogue browser can edit from the list without one round trip per keystroke.

get.summary: Full-text search inside one revision.
get.description: bm25 is SQLite's own score, lower is better, passed through unmodified: a rescaled number invites comparisons across queries and SQLite versions it cannot support. A query shorter than the trigram minimum takes the prefix-scan path and scores 0, which is the store's honest this-was-not-ranked value.

get.summary: One message with its display pages.

patch.summary: Edit the speech rendering. original_text is not writable here.
patch.description: If-Match carries the profile revision's row version, which is the unit of concurrency: the store moves it exactly once per write, so two editors of one revision cannot silently overwrite each other (ADR-0015). A published or archived revision answers 409. A body carrying original_text answers 400 rather than being ignored.

200.description: Edited. ETag is the revision's new token.

get.summary: A revision's roster.

post.summary: Link an import's speaker placeholder to a character.
post.description: The curator's identification of an opaque source speaker (ADR-0070): the placeholder {cid} — the row an import created for a speaker id the source names only as an attribute — is identified as the target character. One transaction re-points the placeholder's lines at the target (confirmed at 1.0, the source-field evidence kept and the acting curator added as a reviewer entry), records one manual speaker assertion per re-pointed line, folds the placeholder's name into the target's aliases so a re-import binds the key straight to the target, and retires the placeholder. Draft revisions only, and If-Match carries the revision's row version like every profile write: 428 when absent, 412 when stale. A retired placeholder or a retired target answers 409, a self-link or a missing or malformed target_character_id answers 400, and a character the revision does not have answers 404.

parameters.name: cid
parameters.description: The placeholder character the import created for the source speaker id.

200.description: Linked. ETag is the revision's new token.

get.summary: A revision's OCR regions.

put.summary: Replace a draft revision's whole region set.
put.description: If-Match carries the profile revision's row version, the same token the message edit sends back (ADR-0015): 428 when absent, 412 when stale, 409 when the revision is published or archived. The body is exhaustive — a region set is one calibration, not a bag of boxes — and the store advances the set's revision exactly once, so cached detections keyed on it invalidate precisely (docs/spec/09 "edits yield new region-set revision"). Geometry is normalised [0,1] frame fractions; a box running past the frame is a 422 with the finding naming the box.

200.description: Saved. ETag is the revision's new token.

post.summary: OCR one frame against the boxes on the canvas.
post.description: A what-if read, never a write: the editor sends a frame — an uploaded capture (multipart, image part ≤ 4 MB) or a fixture path under the configured replay roots (application/json, fixture) — plus the boxes to read, and gets back per box four OCR variants (PSM 6/7 crossed with preprocess on/off, the settings a profile stores in regions.ocr_settings), the textbox-presence classification the runtime's panel detector applies (docs/spec/04), and the timings the page renders. Boxes default to the revision's stored regions when the request names none. The image is held in memory for the request only; it is persisted exactly when dev_trace is set and an event hub is wired, as a regions.preview event carrying the frame.

fixture.description: A clean relative frame path under the replay roots, e.g. synthetic/textbox/plain-dejavu-01.png. Traversal and absolute paths are refused.

image.description: The capture frame, at most 4 MB.

regions.description: A JSON array of PreviewBox, optional: the revision's stored regions answer when it is absent.

dev_trace.description: true/1 for the dev-trace event; optional.

get.summary: One page of a revision's dialogue graph.
get.description: The virtualized graph's page contract (docs/spec/09): nodes carry the short normalized text (≤ 80 runes) the list row renders, plus the attribution a verified-vs-inferred label needs; edges are returned only when both endpoints are on the page, so a filtered or partial page is a connected subgraph rather than half-edges at its boundary. Filters are exact, server-side matches on speaker, message kind and scene.

200.description: One page of nodes and the edges between them.

post.summary: Upload a script into a draft revision; the parse runs as a job.
post.description: The bytes are hashed and committed to the asset store synchronously, so provenance exists whatever the parser then does, and the parse is queued as an import.file job: its progress and report are at GET /api/v1/jobs/{id} and on the event stream as job.* frames. Re-uploading the same bytes to the same revision reconciles by (source, source_message_id) instead of duplicating (docs/spec/02 Import resume by content hash). Two request shapes are accepted because the two clients differ: a browser sends multipart/form-data with a file part and the mapping as form fields; a script pipes the bytes with a Content-Type and the mapping as query parameters. rights=unknown is refused with 422 JOB_REQUIRES_INPUT rather than stored: a file the user handed over has a known rights position (docs/spec/01 invariant 6).

get.summary: Download this revision as a .gnprofile.json manifest.
get.description: The default is rights-filtered: source pointers are always carried, and text derived from a source whose rights position is unresolved is withheld with a redacted_reason naming why (docs/spec/14). bytes=true additionally packs the source blobs into a .gnpack and needs acknowledge_copyright=true, which is a human decision this API never supplies on a caller's behalf.

200.description: The manifest (application/json), or a .gnpack when bytes=true.

get.summary: The durable queue, newest first.
One job with its attempt history.

post.summary: Cancel a queued or running job (cooperative).
Re-queue a failed or cancelled job.
Start one session: run the published profile against a frame source.
post.description: One active session at a time (docs/spec/01 key invariant). Only the edition's published revision runs. v4l2 and dolphin frame sources answer 501 unsupported_capability; replay directories must sit under the configured allowlist. dev_trace stores sampled frames and ROI crops under a per-session byte quota and additionally requires the caller to hold the developer role on this operator route (docs/spec/13 explicit toggle; ADR-0024).

201.description: Session accepted; state is starting and event_cursor is the session.started seq.

post.summary: Upload a replay clip: an archive of the replay layout, installed under the managed store.
post.description: multipart/form-data with a file part carrying the archive (tar or zip; a single top-level directory is unwrapped) and an optional name field naming the clip id. The archive is committed to the asset store under its content hash before it is extracted; the extraction is confined to a staging directory (zip-slip, symlink and absolute entries are refused); the layout is validated against the replay format (a timestamps.json manifest whose frames exist and whose first and last frame decode); and only then does the clip install under the managed store directory that the session runtime always treats as a replay root — the product path by which a recorded clip reaches a running appliance without an operator editing the service environment (ADR-0073). A colliding id answers 409 clip_exists, never a silent rename.

file.description: The clip archive (tar or zip; gzip-wrapped tar is not admitted), at most 512 MiB, at most 1 GiB uncompressed, at most 50000 entries, at most 64 MiB per file.

name.description: Optional clip id (a lowercase slug of at most 64 characters). Without it the id comes from the archive's top-level directory, then the uploaded filename, then a hash-derived fallback.

201.description: The clip is installed and its provenance recorded.

get.summary: List the managed replay clip store.
get.description: The store's provenance table reconciled against its directories: a directory the index lost is adopted (validated, created_by recovered), and an index row whose directory is gone is listed with missing true. No host path appears in the answer; the id is the whole address a session needs.

200.description: The store's clips, in index order.

delete.summary: Remove one clip from the managed store by id.
delete.description: The id is validated against the clip id contract before any filesystem access. A clip running in an active session is not refused: the session's open files keep reading and the session settles with source-missing. The index row is removed best-effort afterwards; the deletion of the directory is the act.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The clip id (a lowercase slug).

204.description: The clip is removed; no body.

get.summary: One session's current state and pipeline counters.

200.description: The session snapshot, active or finished.

post.summary: Stop a session (idempotent).

200.description: The terminal snapshot when the run has settled.

post.summary: Apply the live audio controls (mute, volume, speech delay) to one session.
post.description: The operator's audio controls of docs/spec/07 (“Apply volume, short fade, optional delay calibration”): mute skips playback but the events still flow (result “muted”), volume scales the samples in the sink path and speech_delay_ms waits before start, still fenced by newer commits. The body is partial: a field left out keeps its current value. The 200 body is the session snapshot with the applied state (Session.audio), not an acknowledgement. A session without a voice pipeline answers 503 audio_unavailable; an out-of-range control (volume outside 0..1, delay outside 0..2000) answers 400 invalid_audio_settings.

200.description: The session snapshot with the applied settings (see Session.audio).

post.summary: Pause a running session (idempotent).
post.description: The operator's pause of docs/spec/08 (“…/pause”). The session's single writer applies it on the same chain as the observations: the commitment policy stops committing (a paused session holds its evidence without deciding), the in-flight recognitions and candidate rankings are cancelled, and the session's speech pipeline fences the audio still queued or playing — a pause pressed mid-line ends that line. The pause is one event (session.paused) on the session's chain, after the cancellations it caused. The 200 body is the session snapshot with paused=true; pausing a paused session is a no-op that returns the same snapshot (a duplicate is not an error the operator needs). A session in a terminal state answers 409 session_not_running: a pause the session cannot take is refused, not dropped.

post.summary: Resume a paused session from the next commit (idempotent).
post.description: The operator's resume of docs/spec/08 (“…/resume”). The session's text machines kept advancing through the pause — the observations were real — so the resume changes no belief: the commitment policy picks up where the evidence stands and the next box that is ready with a valid ranking commits exactly once. A resume can therefore never burst a backlog of the paused window's lines; those decisions were made and are idempotent. The resume is one event (session.resumed) on the session's chain. The 200 body is the session snapshot with paused=false; resuming an unpaused session is a no-op that returns the same snapshot. A session in a terminal state answers 409 session_not_running.

put.summary: Apply the mid-session operator policy: the narrated classes and the decision mode.
put.description: The operator's settings of docs/spec/08 (“…/settings”) and docs/spec/09 (“/play”: the narrated classes “Dialogue / +Signs / +Items” and the Conservative / Predictive toggle). The body is partial: a field left out keeps the session's current value, so a client that only flips the mode never re-sends the classes it never touched. The merged request is validated against the documented vocabulary (mode is conservative or predictive; narrated_classes are the text-kind words) — a value outside it answers 400 invalid_session_settings. The change is one control message to the session's single writer: the decision mode moves the commitment policy and the text machines together, and the narrated classes move the commitment policy's eligibility filter (a committed line whose class is not narrated commits — the box advances and the text machine knows — but is marked not eligible, which is the speech layer's no-audio answer). Every change is one event (session.settings_changed) on the session's chain carrying the applied mode and classes; a request that names the state the session already has is a no-op — no event, because a settings message is an operator-visible change and one that changed nothing would be a lie in the event log. The 200 body is the session snapshot carrying the applied mode and the normalized narrated_classes (dialogue always present, first — the product's default — in the list the UI's toggles read).

200.description: The session snapshot with the applied policy (see Session.mode and Session.narrated_classes).

get.summary: Page the durable event log for the developer inspector.
get.description: REST snapshot of the persisted events (the SSE stream's durable half), filterable by session and name. Payloads carry raw recognised gameplay text and provider details, so the route is developer-only (docs/spec/08: developer mode displays sensitive gameplay text and provider traces).

parameters.name: session_id
parameters.description: Restrict to one session's events.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Restrict to events with this name; repeatable.

parameters.name: since_seq
parameters.description: Resume cursor: first seq to include.

200.description: One page of envelopes in seq order.

get.summary: The process's telemetry snapshot: the metrics the diagnostics and health surfaces read.
get.description: The JSON snapshot of the process's telemetry registry (docs/spec/13 "Metrics", internal/telemetry): the same counters, histograms and gauges the Prometheus scrape at GET /metrics renders, shaped for the appliance's own diagnostics and health surfaces to read without parsing a text stream. Bounded by construction — the label dimensions are the game and the profile revision only (docs/spec/13: aggregate by game/profile revisions, never a per-message label), and each metric keeps at most a fixed number of series. Developer-only, like the other /api/v1/dev inspection routes: the snapshot is the appliance's run state. A process that wired no telemetry catalog answers 503: an empty snapshot would read as "everything is zero."

get.summary: Browse the recorded fixtures.
get.description: The developer's view of the correction labels as the re-run inputs (docs/spec/08 "fixture recording and browsing", docs/spec/09 "save a fixture and inspect a test report"). Same rows and shape as GET /api/v1/corrections; the reading is the difference (ADR-0052).

parameters.name: profile_id
parameters.description: Restrict to one revision's labels.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: Restrict to one correction kind. An unknown kind is a 400, not a dropped filter.

post.summary: Record one trace as a replayable fixture (developer).
post.description: Reads the trace's persisted envelopes and writes one trace fixture under the external fixture root — never into the repository (AGENTS.md rule 5). post.summary: A consistent SQLite backup of the live catalogue, as a download (admin).
post.description: The store's online-backup API writes the snapshot while the live connection keeps serving. The restore half of the pair is the admin route POST /api/v1/admin/restore (ADR-0090): the UI uploads a backup there, the server validates it (format, schema marker, integrity, forward-migrations only), makes a pre-restore safety copy, schedules the swap and restarts the process; the CLI (game-narrator db restore) remains the unattended path.

post.summary: Upload a backup and schedule its restore (admin).
post.description: The UI half of backup/restore (ADR-0090, docs/spec/09). The multipart upload carries one backup file (at most 256 MiB). The server validates it before touching anything: SQLite format, the schema_migrations marker (an ordinary database is refused), integrity (PRAGMA integrity_check), and schema — a backup newer than this binary is refused (it must be opened by the release that wrote it), an older one is migrated forward by the normal boot path. Then it writes a pre-restore copy of the live store into the backups directory (the rollback artifact, named in the 202 body), schedules the swap (a plan file in the data directory) and answers 202; the process then runs its normal graceful shutdown, and the replacement's boot applies the swap: the backup is installed over the live file and forward-migrated, and a swap that fails after touching the file recovers the live database from the pre-restore copy, so a bad restore degrades to the pre-restore state rather than a dead appliance. Under the documented deployment (the systemd unit) the replacement is back within seconds; without a supervisor the plan stays pending and the status route says exactly that. Errors (400 malformed upload, 413 oversize, 422 backup-invalid / backup-newer-than-binary, 503 with no store or no restart wired) leave the store untouched. Nothing here is silent: every step is on the event stream as admin.restore.* (admin scope).

backup.description: The backup file produced by POST /api/v1/admin/backup (at most 256 MiB).

202.description: The restore is scheduled and the appliance is shutting down to apply it.

get.summary: What the last restore did, or that one is pending (admin).
get.description: The status half of the restore pair (ADR-0090). The UI polls this after the restart: status is none (no restore ever ran and none is pending), pending (a plan is waiting for the next boot), applied or failed. A failed swap that touched the file carries recovered_from_pre_restore: the live database was recovered from the pre-restore copy, so the appliance serves the pre-restore state rather than a dead one. The plan's identity fields (hash, size, schema versions, actor, request id) are the audit facts; absolute paths stay server-side.

get.summary: One throttled JPEG preview snapshot of the capture device (operator).
get.description: The preview (ADR-0078): one JPEG frame through a throwaway source — build, start, one frame, encode at quality 60 capped to 1280 px wide, close. The device query parameter names a stable id; absent, the stack's own resolution (the persisted selection, then the first usable device). The route is authenticated and globally throttled: one snapshot in flight and a 500 ms minimum interval, answered 429 with Retry-After when exceeded (docs/spec/08 rate-limits preview streaming). It is also refused 503 capture-busy while a running session holds the same device — the UVC bus is single-consumer, and the answer names the holding session.

parameters.name: device
parameters.description: The capture device's stable id (from listCaptureDevices); absent, the persisted selection then the first usable device.

200.description: The JPEG snapshot of the device.

400.description: The requested device is not in the current enumeration.

429.description: The preview is throttled (one in flight, 500 ms apart); Retry-After says when to try again.

503.description: No usable device is attached, the device is held by a running session (capture-busy), or the device is not delivering frames.

post.summary: Run the capture test: grab frames, report freshness/drops, OCR the region (operator).
post.description: The docs/spec/10 capture test (ADR-0078): grab `frames` (default 20, capped 200) from a throwaway source on the resolved device, report grabbed / dropped / fps / freshness_ms / state / last_error (the freshness and dropped-frame checks), and OCR the requested region (a pixel box; absent, the centre third) of the last frame with the region editor's Tesseract engine. OCR is degradable: a missing engine degrades the ocr block to engine 'unavailable' with the install action, never failing a probe whose frame stats are valid. The device is held 503 capture-busy while a running session runs it.

200.description: The probe report: the frame stats and the OCR block.

400.description: The requested device is not in the current enumeration, or the body is not valid.

503.description: No usable device is attached, the device is held by a running session (capture-busy), or the device is not delivering frames.

get.summary: The correction labels, newest first.
get.description: User fixes recorded as labels (docs/spec/08 "user fixes become labels"): the dialogue editor records a speech_text correction inside its save (ADR-0052), and explicit recordings arrive through POST. The list is the curation-side reading of the same rows the developer browses as fixtures.

parameters.name: profile_id
parameters.description: Restrict to one revision's labels.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: Restrict to one correction kind. An unknown kind is a 400, not a dropped filter.

post.summary: Record a correction (a label only; it applies no fix).
post.description: The inspector's correction actions and anything else that records a user fix. The label lands as proposed with the caller as actor; a message target must name an existing row of the revision. It never applies the fix — applying is the corresponding content write (ADR-0052).

get.summary: List the disc images in the allowlisted import directory.
get.description: What a curator can import from the directory the operator names with GAME_NARRATOR_IMPORT_DIR: the regular files directly in it, by basename with size and mtime. The API never answers with the directory's own path (AGENTS.md rule 5), and symlinks the operator placed in the directory are listed like any other file. An unconfigured directory is a state, not a fault: the route answers 200 with configured:false and an empty list, and the upload shape of POST /profiles/{id}/import/disc is then the import path. 503 SUBSYSTEM_UNAVAILABLE remains for a build whose dependencies are unwired and for a configured directory that cannot be read.

200.description: The regular files directly in the directory, sorted by name.

post.summary: Import a game's script from a disc image; the hash, parse and write run as a job.
post.description: Two request shapes, one 202 body (ADR-0066). Dir shape: a JSON body {"image": "<basename>"} (or ?image=<name>) naming a regular file in the allowlisted import directory; the job reads the image in place and never copies it, so a crash resumes against the same on-disk image. Upload shape: multipart/form-data with a file part carrying the raw image (CISO or plain GCM), streamed into the asset store under the shared upload cap with its hash computed while streaming — real GB-scale discs do not fit the cap by design, and the 202 detail says the directory is the full-image path. The target revision must be a draft (409 otherwise, as on the file import). The job (kind import.disc) opens the image, lets the disc-capable adapter verify the game id and extract the message script, and imports it through the same machinery as the file import: the BMG is content-addressed, a re-import of the same image reconciles by hash instead of duplicating, and the result is a DiscImportReport. The image path is never logged or stored; the report and the source row carry the image's SHA-256 and the game id instead.

requestBody.description: Dir shape: application/json with {"image": "<basename>"}. Upload shape: multipart/form-data with a file part named `file`.

file.description: the raw disc image (CISO or plain GCM)

post.summary: Send one dock message (a new thread or a turn in an existing one).
post.description: The text and the screen context are rendered into one user turn; with a thread_id the turn is appended to that thread's durable conversation, without one a new thread (and its durable agent run) is opened and the turn is the attempt's opening request. The attempt runs as the assistant.run job kind and the reply streams over the event hub (assistant.message for the narrative, assistant.question for NEEDS-YOU and confirmation cards, the loop's step and tool events for the cards' tail). 409 while an attempt for the thread is already queued or running.

202.description: The turn is stored and the attempt queued.

post.summary: Answer a NEEDS-YOU question or confirmation.
post.description: The answer becomes a durable user message in the thread's conversation and marks the question row answered (UX-04: the question never blocked the run; this is when the answer is applied). Exactly one follow-up attempt is owed: this call enqueues it when no attempt is in flight and names it in job_id; while an attempt is in flight its post-run hook enqueues it instead and job_id is absent. A confirmation's answer is confirm or cancel; an empty answer defers the question. 404 for a question that is not in the caller's thread; 422 for an invalid confirmation answer.

202.description: The answer is durable and the follow-up is owed.

get.summary: List the caller's assistant threads, newest first.
get.description: Cursor-paginated (next_cursor, empty on the last page). Each thread shows the state of its durable run, so the dock can show which threads are mid-attempt.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The next_cursor from a previous page.

get.summary: Read one assistant thread's snapshot.
get.description: The conversation tail (user and assistant turns), the questions (open NEEDS-YOU cards and recent answers) and the tool cards (the run's executed tool calls with state, duration and a result preview). A page that missed the event stream rebuilds from this; a thread the caller does not own is a 404, not a 403.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The thread ULID.

post.summary: Duplicate a revision: a new draft of the same edition with its content snapshot (FR-02).
post.description: The lifecycle verb over the revision-snapshot store primitive (ADR-0107): every row gets a fresh id, internal references are rewritten, corrections and publication history are not copied, and parent_revision records the derivation. Audited as catalog.profile.duplicate so the intent stays distinguishable from POST .../revisions.

post.summary: Clone a revision into a new game with a matching edition and a draft revision 1 (FR-02).
post.description: One store transaction: the new game (caller's title/slug or the source's, slug suffixed -copy, -2, ... until free), the edition copy, the draft revision with the content snapshot, and the clone_links provenance row (ADR-0107). The source must not be deleted. Audited as catalog.profile.clone.

201.description: The clone: the new game, edition, draft revision and the provenance link.

post.summary: Purge a soft-deleted revision after its retention window (admin).
post.description: The admin half of the two-step delete (ADR-0107). Requires now >= purge_after (409 RETENTION_NOT_ELAPSED before the window closes), re-checks the soft-delete guards, then in one store transaction deletes the profile's speech-cache rows and the profile row (the content cascades, the FTS triggers follow). After the commit the now-unreferenced blobs are removed under the reference-before-delete discipline (ADR-0041). Audited as catalog.profile.purge.

200.description: The purge report: the cache entries removed and the blobs deleted.

post.summary: Disable a game: hidden from Play and narration, still editable (FR-02).
post.description: Sets games.disabled (ADR-0107): session start refuses any of its profiles with 409 GAME_DISABLED, while every catalogue write on the game keeps working and the game stays in the library list with disabled: true. Audited as catalog.game.disable.

post.summary: Re-enable a disabled game (FR-02).
post.description: Clears games.disabled (ADR-0107): the game is playable again and session start accepts its profiles. Audited as catalog.game.enable.

gnSession.name: gn_session
gnSession.description: HttpOnly SameSite=Strict session cookie minted by POST /api/v1/auth/login.

csrfToken.name: X-CSRF-Token
csrfToken.description: Required with the session cookie on every unsafe method. Ignored for bearer-token callers, which a browser cannot attach cross-site.

bearerToken.description: Authorization: Bearer gn_…, minted by POST /api/v1/users/{id}/tokens or game-narrator admin token.

UserId.name: id
UserId.description: Account ULID. A malformed id answers 404, the same as an unknown one, so the route cannot enumerate id shapes.

IdempotencyKeyOptional.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKeyOptional.description: Honoured durably here rather than in the process's memory: the queue's unique idempotency_key column stores it, scoped to kind + principal + revision, so a retry after a dropped 202 gets the same job back instead of a second parse. Sending the same key with different bytes is a 422. The response cannot be replayed from a cache because the work may still be running; the job resource is the answer (ADR-0017).

Cursor.name: cursor
Cursor.description: An opaque next_cursor issued by this service for the same list. Anything else is a 400, not an empty page.

Limit.name: limit
Limit.description: Hard upper bound 200. Out-of-range is refused rather than clamped: a clamped limit makes a client's 'give me everything' look successful while it silently received 50.

SearchLimit.name: limit
SearchLimit.description: Search hits carry whole message rows, so the ceiling is tighter than a list's.

GraphLimit.name: limit
GraphLimit.description: The graph page virtualizes, so its ceiling is the 2 000 nodes docs/spec/09 bounds the view at, and an omitted limit is one list-pane pageful, not the whole revision.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: At most 200 characters. Same key + same body replays the stored response; same key + different body is a 422. Held in the process's memory only: a restart forgets it, and a retried POST then lands on the store's own uniqueness rules instead (ADR-0017).

SessionId.name: id
SessionId.description: The session id returned by POST /api/v1/sessions (a ULID).

TraceId.name: trace_id
TraceId.description: The trace id correlating one decision across events (docs/spec/09).

AssetSha256.name: sha256
AssetSha256.description: Lowercase hex sha256 of a stored dev-trace sample, as referenced by frame_asset or crop_asset on text.observed.

VoiceId.name: id
VoiceId.description: Voice revision ULID. A malformed id answers 404, the same as an unknown one.

AuditionId.name: aid
AuditionId.description: Audition clip ULID on the named revision.

CorrectionsLimit.name: limit
CorrectionsLimit.description: Hard upper bound 500; omitted means 100. Out-of-range is refused rather than clamped (docs/spec/08 "hard upper bounds").

BtMac.name: mac
BtMac.description: The device's Bluetooth MAC in colon form (AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF; case-insensitive, the answer echoes the normalised upper-case form). A malformed address is a 400 invalid-mac - the API never sends a typo to the radio.

Problem.description: RFC 9457 problem+json. code is the stable member of docs/spec/08's error contract; X-Request-Id correlates it with the server log and the event stream.

MetricsSnapshot.description: The GET /api/v1/dev/metrics body (docs/spec/13 "Metrics", internal/telemetry): the process's telemetry registry as a structured view — the same data the Prometheus exposition at GET /metrics renders, shaped for the diagnostics and health surfaces to read. generated_at is the process wall clock (the freshness of the reading, not a metric).

MetricSnapshot.description: One metric and every series it currently holds. type is the Prometheus kind; the series carry the label pair (game, profile_revision) for counters and histograms and no labels for the process-wide gauges.

MetricSeries.description: One labelled series. A counter or gauge row carries value; a histogram row carries count, sum_seconds and the non-cumulative buckets. Absent fields encode as absent, so a counter row carries no buckets and a histogram row no value.

labels.description: The bounded label set (game, profile_revision); absent for a process-wide gauge.

value.description: The counter total or the gauge reading.

sum_seconds.description: The histogram sample sum, in seconds.

buckets.description: The histogram's non-cumulative slots: one per bucket edge, plus the overflow slot whose le is null (the exposition's le=+Inf row).

MetricHistogramBucket.description: One histogram slot. le is the bucket edge in seconds; null is the overflow slot (le=+Inf in the exposition).

Problem.description: An RFC 9457 problem document. `code` is the stable member of docs/spec/08's error contract and is present on every problem the catalog, profile, message and import handlers of ADR-0017 write; the authorization gate and the router's 404/405 (internal/api/middleware.go, ADR-0016) predate it and answer without one, so it is documented here rather than required.

instance.description: The request path that produced it.

code.description: One of: RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND, RESOURCE_CONFLICT, VALIDATION_FAILED, PROFILE_REVISION_CONFLICT, PROFILE_IMMUTABLE, PROFILE_TRANSITION_INVALID, CONTENT_RIGHTS_REVIEW_REQUIRED, UNKNOWN_GAME_EDITION, JOB_REQUIRES_INPUT, IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED, IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED, UPLOAD_TOO_LARGE, INVALID_PARAMETER, NOT_SUPPORTED, SUBSYSTEM_UNAVAILABLE, INTERNAL.

problems.description: Every finding, for the publish gate and the importer report (docs/spec/03's review screen).

User.description: No field can hold a password hash or a token digest.

Game.description: A title family (docs/spec/02 Entity catalog: games). Metadata only: no row version, no content.

disabled.description: games.disabled (ADR-0107): the title family's library switch. A disabled game is hidden from Play (session start refuses its profiles with 409 GAME_DISABLED) while its profiles stay editable and the game stays in the library list with the flag on.

source_identity.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256, or empty when no image was observed.

ProfileStatus.description: draft is editable; review is frozen for approval; published is immutable and what sessions pin; archived stays addressable but is no longer selectable. Archived is terminal.

Profile.description: One revision of one edition. row_version is not a field: it is the ETag header (quoted decimal), which is what If-Match carries back.

manifest_digest.description: Empty until a publication has computed it. It is also the first component of every audio cache key.

narrator_fallback.description: profiles.narrator_fallback (ADR-0101): whether a line whose speaker has no approved voice is spoken by the narrator voice. Always present; on by default.

next_states.description: The lifecycle moves this revision can still make, from the transition table.

deleted_at.description: The soft-delete mark (ADR-0107): present only on the DELETE receipt and on the store-side rows during the retention window; the API surfaces hide marked revisions (the list omits them, the direct read 404s).

purge_after.description: The retention deadline (ADR-0107): deleted_at + 72h. Before it, the purge answers 409 RETENTION_NOT_ELAPSED.

PublishAction.description: One entry of an edition's publication history: what shipped, what it retired, who decided, which digest was validated, and what the gate found.

detail.description: The writer's own context as a JSON document, e.g. {"via":"SetProfileStatus"}.

TextKind.description: messages.text_kind: the content class that selects OCR defaults and speech rendering style.

RightsStatus.description: What may be done with a source's bytes. unknown is never accepted on an upload and never publishable (docs/spec/14).

AttributionStatus.description: The confidence ladder behind speaker_id, kept separate from it: a name on screen is evidence, not a foreign key (docs/spec/02).

Message.description: Canonical source text plus its renderings (messages). Not an occurrence, a page, an utterance or an audio asset.

source_id.description: Absent when no source row backs the line, which is always the case for a manual entry.

source_message_id.description: The source-side identity re-imports reconcile on. Present whenever source_id is.

original_text.description: Exactly what the source said. Read-only through this API.

speech_text.description: The curator's speaking rendering. The only writable text field.

MessagePage.description: One display page of a message (message_pages). A page is not an utterance.

MessageDetail.description: One message plus its display pages. pages is [] rather than absent when the message has none.

bm25.description: SQLite's bm25, lower is better. 0 means the prefix-scan path did not rank this hit.

portrait_asset_id.description: A content hash, not a path: the bytes live in the asset store (ADR-0014).

status.description: characters.status (games.CharacterStatus). Retired, not rejected: a name the reviewer decided against stays out of the roster rather than becoming a denial of the source.

Region.description: One named rectangle of the screen where text is read. Rect* are normalised [0,1] fractions of the display frame, so aspect conversion stays in the adapter (docs/spec/04).

payload.description: The job's inputs as JSON, passed through rather than re-encoded.

result.description: The job's outcome or structured error.

trace_id.description: The correlation id its events carry.

JobDetail.description: A job plus the attempt history that makes a crash visible (docs/spec/13). It is spelled out rather than composed with allOf over Job, because the two shapes genuinely disagree on one member: internal/api/jobs.go's jobDetailResponse embeds the list DTO (whose `attempts` is an integer retry counter) and then re-declares `attempts` as the history array, and encoding/json keeps the shallower field — so the detail response carries the history and *not* the count, which only the list gives. ADR-0017 records that as a deviation owned by the queue milestone's file rather than renaming it from here.

attempts.description: The attempt history, not the retry count: see the schema description.

ImportAccepted.description: The upload is durable and the parse is queued. Progress and the parse report are the job's.

sha256.description: The content address the bytes were committed under.

media_type.description: Sniffed from the bytes, never from a caller-supplied header.

ImportReport.description: The result_json of a succeeded import.file job: what the parse saw, in the shape docs/spec/03's review screen reads.

adapter.description: id@semver, so which importer build produced these rows stays answerable (docs/spec/04).

ProfileManifest.description: The .gnprofile.json document (docs/spec/17 formalised, docs/spec/02 Profile portability). It carries source *pointers* and rights-filtered text; the bytes themselves never travel by default.

schema_version.description: 1.1 adds the voices section and publication.narrator_fallback (ADR-0101).

narrator_fallback.description: profiles.narrator_fallback (ADR-0101): when a line's speaker has no approved voice, the narrator voice speaks the line if and only if this is true. A re-import applies it to the draft it creates; the import's default when absent is true.

voices.description: Approved voice revisions (ADR-0101). Each row keeps its stable id (the registry name and speech cache key derive from it) and carries the reference SHA-256, fingerprint, consent and provenance. The reference WAV bytes travel only inside a .gnpack.

manifest_digest.description: A fingerprint of content, computed so it survives a re-import's id remapping.

GameList.description: One page of the library. `next_cursor` is present exactly when another page exists: an absent member is the end of the walk, not an empty page. A token this service did not issue is a 400.

EditionList.description: Every edition of one game. Unpaginated by decision: a title has a handful (region × language × disc revision), and internal/store/repo_catalog.go reads them as one slice.

ProfileList.description: Every revision of one edition, lowest revision_num first.

MessageList.description: One page of a revision's dialogue. `profile_etag` is the revision's current If-Match token, so the dialogue browser can edit straight from this page instead of fetching the profile once per keystroke. It is the same integer as the profile's ETag header, from the same row — a convenience member, not a second token.

profile_etag.description: Quoted decimal row_version, identical to the ETag of GET /api/v1/profiles/{id}.

MessageSearchResult.description: A ranked hit list. A phrase that occurs nowhere is an empty array, never a 404: silence and absence are different facts and the browser must show the second one.

query.description: Echoed so a client can tell which search this page answers.

SearchResponse.description: The ⌘K palette's one response (ADR-0098). groups is always an array, never null: an empty array is the honest nothing-matched, and the omitted-group rule means the array is empty only when every requested kind missed.

query.description: The normalised query (trimmed, internal whitespace collapsed), echoed for the list header.

agent_prompt.description: Always equal to query after normalisation; present so the Tab key has one source of truth to hand to the agent dock instead of re-deriving it.

SearchResult.description: One palette row. Exactly one of route and action is present: the row either navigates or it executes. score is higher-is-better within the row's group (see the operation's description).

id.description: The entity's id, or verb-id:entity-id for action rows.

subtitle.description: The second line of the row: the game a character or line belongs to, the platform of a game, or what an action does.

SearchAction.description: The API call an action row executes on ↵ instead of navigating.

CharacterList.description: One revision's roster. Always an array, never null: a generated client typed as Character[] must not receive null.

SpeakerLinkRequest.description: The identification itself: which live character the placeholder is. A self-link is refused with 400.

target_character_id.description: The character the placeholder's speaker is identified as.

SpeakerLinkResponse.description: The link's outcome, counts only: which rows were joined and how many lines moved.

profile_id.description: The revision the link was recorded on.

source_character_id.description: The placeholder, now retired; its name is folded into the target's aliases.

target_character_id.description: The character the placeholder is identified as.

repointed_messages.description: The lines that now point at the target, each confirmed at 1.0 with a manual assertion.

RegionList.description: One revision's region set — every rectangle text is read from, with the values that may be null because the source did not state them.

RegionSetInput.description: The region set a draft editor saves: every box on the canvas, exhaustive, in normalized [0,1] frame fractions. Omitted ids are minted by the service; omitted constraints stay unconstrained.

RegionInput.description: One box as the editor sends it. x+w and y+h must stay ≤ 1: the same box-inside-the-frame rule the regions table's CHECK enforces.

id.description: A region id from a previous GET, or omitted for a new box (the service mints one).

scene_id.description: The scene this box is calibrated against; empty for a set-wide box.

min_aspect.description: The capture constraints the preset picker fills in: the region only reads inside this aspect band and at or above these source pixels. Null when omitted.

ocr_settings.description: The OCR engine settings for this crop (scale, threshold, PSM, whitelist) the adapter interprets. Defaults to {}.

mask_asset_ids.description: Asset hashes holding occlusion/crop masks. Defaults to [].

reliability.description: Measured reliability on [0,1]; null until a fixture run measures it.

RegionSet.description: The stored set a replace wrote: the rows with server-assigned timestamps and the set revision the edit advanced.

revision.description: The region-set revision this save stamped (0002's regions.revision, one number per set).

GraphList.description: One page of a revision's dialogue graph (docs/spec/09 "/games/:id/graph"): the nodes the virtualized list renders plus every edge whose two endpoints both land on the page.

total.description: The filtered node count, for the page's "n of m" line.

GraphNode.description: One list row of the graph. text is the normalized text cut to the row's 80-rune label; speaker and scene are null for the unattributed and un-scene lines, which the page renders by name absence.

attribution_status.description: The verified-vs-inferred label the page renders (docs/spec/09 "UX robustness").

GraphEdge.description: One dialogue transition with its provenance: the kind the legend colours, the confidence that ranks it, the source row that established it and how many observations back it (docs/spec/04 "Dialogue graph").

source.description: The source row that established the transition, null when the graph builder inferred it.

evidence.description: The backing observations' count, derived from the stored evidence array.

condition.description: The data-only condition expression (0002's condition_expr); absent for edges without one.

PreviewBox.description: One canvas box: normalized [0,1] geometry plus the stored region's id when the box edits a saved row.

PreviewResult.description: The OCR preview: per-box variants (PSM 6/7 crossed with preprocess on/off), the textbox-presence classification, and timings. The image itself never appears outside the dev-trace event the caller opts into.

fixture_path.description: The fixture path as admitted, for the dev-trace line; absent on uploads.

engine.description: The engine that produced the variants (tesseract).

duration_ms.description: Wall-clock of the whole preview, every box and variant.

textbox_verdict.description: The classification the page headlines: present when any box's panel detector fired.

dev_trace.description: Set when the regions.preview event was stored with this preview.

PreviewRegion.description: One box's preview result. A variant's error is carried in the variant, not thrown: the page's job is to show which setting reads the box and which does not.

empty.description: The box covered nothing at this resolution: a different fact from a box that is there and blank.

PreviewPresence.description: The textbox-presence classification: the runtime's panel detector (a crop is a panel when the share of its pixels below the dark-luma threshold reaches the minimum), measured on the raw crop the runtime measures on.

PreviewVariant.description: One (PSM, preprocess) cell of the preview matrix: what that setting reads, how confident it is, how long it took, or why it failed.

psm.description: 6 (uniform text block) or 7 (single line): the two PSMs the preview matrix runs (docs/spec/05).

preprocess.description: Whether the crop went through the pipeline's preprocess steps (scale, threshold, auto-invert) before the engine saw it.

text.description: The engine's reading, raw: normalization is the caller's step, as the pipeline keeps it (docs/spec/05).

error.description: Set when this cell failed (engine missing, timeout, failed read): the other cells still answer.

PublishActionList.description: An edition's publication history, newest first: what shipped, what it retired, what was refused and which findings refused it (docs/spec/16 answers those from the database).

JobList.description: One page of the durable queue.

SessionMode.description: docs/spec/01: conservative commits only on the documented evidence bar; predictive may commit earlier at higher risk.

FrameSourceKind.description: replay reads a recording directory from the configured allowlist; test_pattern is the built-in synthetic source; v4l2 is the UVC HDMI capture dongle (ADR-0078) — dir is the device's stable id (empty: the persisted selection, then the first usable device); dolphin is the dev-only emulator bridge (ADR-0007) and answers 501 unsupported_capability unless its dev gate is met.

dir.description: The replay recording directory for kind replay (required, under the configured allowlist); for kind v4l2 the capture device stable id (ADR-0078; empty = the persisted selection, then the first usable device).

clip_id.description: A managed-store clip id (from GET /api/v1/replay/clips); with kind replay it selects the clip by id and outranks dir. The id is validated against the clip id contract and its resolved directory still has to pass the replay-root allowlist (ADR-0073).

profile_id.description: The profile to run; must be the edition's published revision.

dev_trace.description: Store sampled frames (downscaled full-frame JPEG, width 640 max) and ROI crop PNGs under the per-session byte quota; requires the caller to hold the developer role.

PipelineStats.description: The pipeline's in-memory self-report: the numbers docs/spec/16's session gate reads.

stale_generation_applied.description: Must stay 0: the generation fence is absolute (docs/spec/01 invariant 2).

audio_underruns.description: Started playbacks that then ended in a sink failure (ADR-0074, docs/spec/13 "playback underruns").

audio_output_latency.description: The output-latency table: sink accepted the playback → the device buffer accepted the first samples. Count 0 when the sink does not report first-sample timestamps.

Session.description: A session's lifecycle state and counters (the API view of the runtime).

reason.description: Terminal reason: requested, source_end, error or closed.

event_cursor.description: The session.started seq; later session events resume from here.

source.description: The capture source's own self-report: whether it is delivering frames at all, and if not, why (docs/spec/13). The pipeline's downstream counters cannot name this fault: a session whose capture child keeps failing reads running with zero frames delivered, and this field carries the source's state and last failure text.

audio.description: Present when the process has a voice workflow wired and this session's sink built; absent on a silent session, where the audio route answers 503 audio_unavailable.

clip_id.description: The managed-store clip this run replays (ADR-0073); absent on dir- and device-sourced sessions.

paused.description: The operator's pause state (docs/spec/08 “…/pause, …/resume”): true while the session has stopped committing and speaking. It moves on the pause/resume routes and the snapshot carries it, so the UI's pause button shows the state the server holds, not the click the operator made.

narrated_classes.description: The operator's narrated-class setting (docs/spec/09 “/play”): the text classes the commitment policy narrates, normalized — dialogue first, always present. The default (dialogue alone) is what a session started without a settings call carries; PUT /api/v1/sessions/{id}/settings moves them.

capture_device.description: The UVC HDMI capture device's stable id this run uses (kind v4l2, ADR-0078): the device the resolution settled on — the requested id, the persisted selection, or the first usable device. Absent for every other source kind.

capture_mode.description: The mode the session asked of that device (e.g. "640x480 MJPEG @ 10 fps"); absent for every other source kind.

capture_mode_source.description: The mode's provenance: the operator's pin or the ADR-0076 policy; absent for every other source kind.

SessionSource.description: The session's capture source self-report (the API view of capture.Stats): the source's own ID and lifecycle state, its delivered count and measured rate, the supervised-restart count that separates a one-time device loss from flapping capture, and the last failure text.

id.description: The source's stable identity (e.g. x11::96+0,0 or replay:dialogue-advance-001).

state.description: The source lifecycle state: starting, running, reconnecting, stopped or failed.

delivered.description: Frames the source has handed to the session since start.

restarts.description: Supervised (re)starts after the first, including failed spawn attempts.

fps.description: Measured arrival rate over the trailing window; zero until enough frames have arrived.

last_frame_at.description: The wall time of the newest delivered frame; absent before the first frame.

last_error.description: The most recent failure text, kept because docs/spec/13 requires an actionable operator action; absent while healthy.

SessionBottlenecks.description: The GET /api/v1/dev/sessions/{id}/bottlenecks body: the session's own per-stage latency summary (docs/spec/16 M7 "diagnostics expose bottlenecks"). The same rows, shares and named slowest stage the support bundle's bottlenecks.json and the developer page read, all computed by the one shared function (runtime.Bottlenecks) from the session's own stats.

slowest_stage.description: The proper sub-stage (capture→OCR or OCR→rank) with the largest p95 — the stage that owns the most of the end-to-end latency. The end-to-end stage is the baseline, never a candidate (it contains both sub-stages); when no sub-stage has samples but the end-to-end stage does, it is named instead. Empty string when no stage has samples.

audio_underruns.description: The run's audio underruns (ADR-0074); present only when the caller attached the audio counters.

audio_output_latency.description: The run's output-latency table (ADR-0074); present only when the caller attached the audio counters.

StageLatency.description: One measured stage of one run's own pipeline latency stats (internal/pipeline: frame_to_ocr, ocr_to_ranked, frame_to_committed). p50_ns and p95_ns are histogram bucket edges (the pipeline buckets by design); max_ns is exact. Wall-clock measurement: a diagnostic, not a verdict (ADR-0064).

stage.description: The stage: capture → OCR, OCR → rank, or capture → committed (the end-to-end baseline).

count.description: How many samples the stage's histogram held.

share_of_end_to_end.description: p95(stage) / p95(frame_to_committed): the stage's share of the end-to-end latency at the p95 point. 1 for the end-to-end stage itself; 0 when the stage or the end-to-end stage has no samples. The ratio of two histogram bucket edges over two different sample populations, so it can exceed 1 when both p95s are quantized edges of sub-millisecond intervals (the honest reading: this stage's p95 edge is above the end-to-end p95 edge).

SessionAudioSettings.description: The live audio controls of POST /api/v1/sessions/{id}/audio. Every field is optional and applied when present; a field left out keeps its current value.

muted.description: Skip playback. The voice still resolves and the audio still synthesises (the cache is filled); the utterance ends with result “muted” instead of starting.

volume.description: Scale the samples in the sink path (1.0 = unity). Outside 0..1 is a 400 invalid_audio_settings.

speech_delay_ms.description: Wait this long before starting playback; the wait is fenced, a newer commit during the delay still cancels the waiting utterance.

SessionSettings.description: The mid-session operator policy of PUT /api/v1/sessions/{id}/settings (docs/spec/08 “…/settings”, docs/spec/09 “/play”). Every field is optional and applied when present; a field left out keeps the session's current value. The applied change is one event (session.settings_changed) on the session's chain, and the answer is the snapshot carrying the applied mode and the normalized narrated_classes.

narrated_classes.description: The text classes the session may narrate. The commitment policy force-includes dialogue (the product), so a request for “signs only” applies as “dialogue and signs”; the normalized list — dialogue first, deduped — is what the snapshot carries. An unknown text-kind word is a 400 invalid_session_settings.

SessionAudio.description: The session's audio half: the sink in use, the live controls, the speech counters and the current utterance (docs/spec/07, docs/spec/13 “did it speak, and why not”).

sink.description: The audio sink the utterances play on.

master_volume.description: The appliance's device-level master volume (ADR-0074), shared by every session of the process.

underruns.description: This run's started playbacks that ended in a sink failure — the docs/spec/13 "playback underruns" counter for this session.

output_latency.description: This run's output-latency table (sink accepted → device first samples); count 0 when the sink does not report first-sample timestamps.

current_utterance.description: The session's current audio position; absent until the first speech event.

SpeechCounters.description: One session's speech decision counters (docs/spec/13): the counts that make “did it speak, and why not” answerable.

requested.description: Commits the speech pipeline was asked to speak.

ready.description: Utterances for which audio was resolved (cache or TTS).

started.description: Playbacks the scheduler started on a sink.

cancelled.description: Cancellations announced (new commit, stale generation, session end).

ended.description: Utterances that reached a terminal state — natural end, failure, skip or mute.

cache_hits.description: Resolutions served from the TTS cache.

UtteranceState.description: The last speech lifecycle step any utterance of the session went through.

result.description: The terminal payload result when the phase is terminal (ended, muted, skipped, failed).

generation.description: The committing generation of the utterance.

utterance_id.description: The dialogue occurrence the audio belongs to.

EventEnvelope.description: The documented event wire shape (docs/spec/08 event stream).

DevEventsPage.description: One page of the durable event log for the developer inspector.

truncated.description: true when the page holds exactly the limit (or more matches existed for a trace).

OnboardingRunRequest.description: Start an onboarding run: the agent onboards this title into a draft profile, as a durable agent.run job.

use_web.description: Allow the agent to research on the web (untrusted sources). Default true.

staged_asset_sha256.description: SHA-256 of a script already staged via POST /api/v1/onboarding/uploads.

profile_id.description: An existing draft profile to onboard; when absent the run creates its own game, edition and draft profile.

file_name.description: The staged file's name, for provenance.

OnboardingRunCreated.description: 202: the run is accepted and executing as a durable agent.run job; watch it at GET /api/v1/onboarding/runs/{id} and on the event stream.

text.description: One user turn; the run resumes to read it.

OnboardingAttemptResult.description: A lifecycle answer (message, pause, resume, cancel, approve).

approval_id.description: Present on approve: the human approval grant (the raw token is never on the wire).

id.description: "publish" for the publish boundary, otherwise the tool call id.

provenance.description: Present on a propose_web_import item (ADR-0075): the exact web source the curator is approving.

url.description: The page URL the approval pins.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the raw (pre-decompression) body recorded when the page was fetched; the approved import is refused if the re-fetched body no longer hashes to this value.

rights.description: The source rights position before the approval (a web page registers as unknown; approving records the user's assertion).

OnboardingToolCallView.description: One tool invocation of the run (the UI's tool timeline).

OnboardingSourceView.description: One content source on the draft profile; web sources are marked untrusted (docs/spec/14).

text.description: Conversation text; approval tokens are redacted.

OnboardingPlan.description: The frozen intent of the run, written on the run row at creation.

OnboardingRunState.description: The REST snapshot of a run: state, steps, the tool timeline, sources, quality reports, draft preview and pending review items.

quality_reports.description: The structured source_quality results (docs/spec/03 Dialogue source quality).

review_item_id.description: "publish" for the publish boundary, or the tool call id of a review-required tool.

OnboardingUploadAccepted.description: 201: the bytes are in the asset store under their SHA-256; name it in POST /api/v1/onboarding/runs.

VoiceRevision.description: One voice revision. A revision is immutable once approved: the reference bytes, transcript, design model and consent record are frozen (docs/spec/07, ADR-0005). States move forward only: draft → auditioning → approved → retired.

character.description: The character slug this voice belongs to.

revision.description: Monotonic per character; approving never mutates an earlier revision.

design_instruction.description: The editable voice brief fed to VoiceDesign.

ref_transcript.description: Present once approved: the exact text the reference speaks.

reference_sha256.description: Present once approved: the content identity of the canonical reference.

fingerprint.description: Present once approved: the voice-revision fingerprint that keys the TTS cache (docs/spec/07).

consent_provenance.description: Present once approved: the consent record that gated the freeze (docs/spec/14).

gain.description: The per-voice output gain (ADR-0074, docs/spec/07 "per-voice gain"): the linear factor the runtime applies to this voice's samples at playback, after the cache key is computed — a gain change never re-synthesises and never invalidates the cache. 0 silences the voice, 1 unity (the default), 10 the clipping bound. Always present: the row's 1.0 default reads as "the samples unchanged", never as "no gain".

registrations.description: Present on the detail view: the per-instance registration state.

VoiceGain.description: The per-voice gain update (ADR-0074): one linear factor, 0..10.

VoiceGainSaved.description: The gain answer: the revision id and the gain now stored (the list and detail rows carry the same value from here on).

VoiceAudition.description: One audition clip: a VoiceDesign candidate on a fixed synthetic line (never game text, docs/spec/03). qa_state is the ASR QA verdict (FR-10, ADR 0061): unknown = not run (role unconfigured or endpoint down), passed, or failed = flagged; approval is refused while an audition is failed until a human reviews its qa_wer/qa_transcript evidence.

transcript.description: The synthetic line the clip speaks.

model_id.description: The VoiceDesign checkpoint that produced it.

sha256.description: Content identity of the clip; the address the approval freezes.

origin.description: The provider origin recorded on the audio.

qa_state.description: The ASR QA verdict: unknown (not run — the degraded mode keeps the voice approvable), passed (transcript within the WER bound), or failed (flagged beyond the bound).

qa_wer.description: Word error rate of the read-back against the line, measured on normalized text (0..1+). Present when the check ran.

qa_cer.description: Character error rate of the read-back against the line, measured on normalized text (0..1+). Present when the check ran.

qa_transcript.description: The recognised transcript verbatim from the ASR endpoint; the review evidence on a flagged audition.

qa_model.description: The ASR model id that produced the verdict.

qa_request_id.description: Correlation id of the ASR request (client-minted when the endpoint returns none).

VoiceDetail.description: The full state of one revision: the revision, its audition rows and its registrations.

VoiceRegistration.description: One per-instance registration row (docs/spec/06 VoiceRegistryManager). ready means the instance lists the voice; invalid carries the reason.

registered_name.description: The namespaced name: gn_<voice8>_<character>_v<revision>_<digest8> (or a gn_test_ name in tests).

err.description: Present when state is invalid: why the registration is not usable.

VoiceList.description: One character's revisions (or all of them when the query omits character).

VoiceAuditionsCreateRequest.description: Starts one design attempt: a draft revision plus a job that generates the audition clips.

brief.description: The voice brief fed to VoiceDesign.

count.description: How many synthetic lines to audition; defaults to 3.

VoiceAuditionsCreateResponse.description: The draft revision exists at 202; the clips arrive when the job finishes. Poll the job or GET the revision.
