VoiceApproveRequest.description: Freezes one audition as the canonical reference. consent is required and must be meaningful (docs/spec/14); an empty consent is a 400 CONSENT_REQUIRED.

text.description: The line to synthesise in the approved voice.

DolphinLaunchRequest.description: The launch body. Every member is optional: the game image comes from the process environment only (GAME_NARRATOR_GAME_IMAGE_PATH) and is never accepted here, the user dir is always a fresh isolated dir, and the defaults are the proven config (OGL backend, native resolution, no savestate or movie).

backend.description: The render backend; "OGL" is the proven default on this host (ADR-0007).

width.description: The expected render window width; 0 = the emulator's native size. The resolved geometry wins and is reported in the status.

height.description: The expected render window height; 0 = native.

save_state.description: An optional savestate to load at start (Dolphin --save_state semantics).

movie.description: An optional movie file to run (Dolphin --movie semantics).

DolphinInputRequest.description: The controller input body: a closed set of button and axis names with range-checked values; an unknown name or an out-of-range axis is a 400, not a silent drop. hold_ms is the hold between PRESS and RELEASE; 0 = the bridge default (calibrated against the emulated frame time, not wall-clock game time).

buttons.description: Names: a b x y z start l r up down left right. A true value presses the button for the hold; the bridge releases it afterwards.

axes.description: Names: main_x main_y stick_x stick_y in -1..1 (sticks), l r in 0..1 (triggers). The bridge resets them to neutral after the inject.

hold_ms.description: The hold between PRESS and RELEASE, in milliseconds; 0 = the bridge default (500 ms).

DolphinStatus.description: The bridge's self-report. It carries host paths only where a trusted developer on the box needs them (user_dir), and the game image by SHA-256 and size — the image path itself is never present in any response.

state.description: The lifecycle: stopped (nothing running), launching (Xvfb/emulator coming up), running (render window resolved, frames capturable), failed (last_error names why).

display.description: The private X display (e.g. ":91"); empty when nothing is running.

dolphin_pid.description: The emulator's pid; 0 when not running.

xvfb_pid.description: The bridge-started Xvfb's pid; 0 when not running (a caller-supplied display is the caller's to own and report).

render_window.description: The render window's xwininfo id (hex); re-resolved on demand because batch mode re-parents the framebuffer window when the game takes over.

pipe_device.description: The controller device the pad is mapped to (the isolated user dir's Pipes/pipe1).

pipe_connected.description: Whether the emulator has opened the controller pipe yet (a false value is normal during early boot).

user_dir.description: The fresh isolated Dolphin user dir for this run (never the real ~/.local/share/dolphin-emu).

image_sha256.description: The SHA-256 of the game image the run uses (the provenance; the path itself is never reported).

first_game_frame_at.description: When WaitForGameFrame last reported a real game frame (the entropy/differ predicate, not process existence); zero time when never.

last_error.description: The failure text of the last failed launch (state = failed).

DolphinRegion.description: A pixel rectangle in the X root window: the render window's absolute geometry, resolved via xwininfo (never the whole root).

SettingsModelRole.description: One model role's effective configuration. The base URL is the literal '<configured>' when set (docs/spec/14: the host never reaches the browser) and the token is a presence boolean; the state string carries the NOT CONFIGURED note with the variable to set.

state.description: CONFIGURED, NOT CONFIGURED or NOT AVAILABLE.

reasoning_effort.description: '' means omit the field; the model's default applies.

capabilities.description: openai.Capabilities() findings. null: the API layer holds no live client in this build.

env.description: The variables that control this role.

SettingsGateway.description: The shared-gateway state by presence only: variable names, never values.

bytes.description: null: the cache's blobs are content-addressed inside the asset store and not distinguishable by size.

data_dir.description: The data directory's base name only; the absolute path is a host path and stays server-side.

sink.description: dummy, filesink or pipewire (filesink when the variable is unset).

AudioDevice.description: One enumerated output device (ADR-0074). id is the stable identity the app selects by across reboots: the PipeWire sink NAME or the ALSA device name — never a numeric index.

kind.description: A USB DAC, an HDMI/displayport/optical output, the platform's built-in output, a virtual null sink, a Bluetooth A2DP sink (the bluez_output.<MAC>.1 node, ADR-0091), or none of the five (unknown - reported, never re-classified).

sample_rate.description: The rate the backend reported for the device (e.g. 48000); absent when the backend does not report one.

channels.description: The channel count the backend reported; absent when the backend does not report one.

selected.description: True for the row the effective selection resolves to (the named id, or the platform default when the selection is "default").

platform_default.description: The platform's own default route, marked by the OS, not chosen by the app.

AudioSelection.description: The effective audio output selection with the source of every part (ADR-0074): the page shows what will actually happen and where each part came from (env override, the persisted store value, the built-in default).

device.description: The output device id ("default" = the platform's own routing).

master_volume.description: The device-level master volume (unity the default; 0 the user's silence calibration).

SelectionSource.description: Where one part of the effective selection came from: the environment override, the persisted store value, or the built-in default.

AudioDevices.description: GET /api/v1/audio/devices: one enumeration — the backend that answered, the rows, the synthetic flag (a fake list from the test seam is never mistaken for hardware) and the effective selection.

synthetic.description: True when the list came from the test seam (GAME_NARRATOR_AUDIO_FAKE_DEVICES): the UI label and the doctor read it.

note.description: A backend-level finding the caller surfaces ("pactl is on PATH but the server is not running", "aplay -L failed") — an empty list with no note would read as "nothing is attached" when the truth is "I could not ask".

TestToneRequest.description: POST /api/v1/audio/test-tone. Consent is the gate: the tone plays only on the page's explicit action (docs/spec/13 makes playback a consented action).

device.description: An enumerated device id to probe; absent, the selected device plays.

TestToneResponse.description: POST /api/v1/audio/test-tone: what the tone endpoint did, with the tone's constants (the one shared spelling the live check asserts) and the sink/device it played on.

level.description: The tone's linear amplitude (0.25, about -12 dB).

evidence_file.description: The tone's recorded WAV (basename) when the sink is the filesink: on a machine with no audible output the file is the proof.

AudioSettingsUpdate.description: PUT /api/v1/settings/audio: the partial body. Every field is optional; a field left out keeps the stored value.

device.description: The output device id ("default" or an enumerated id).

AudioSettingsAnswer.description: PUT /api/v1/settings/audio: the row now stored and the effective selection (env overrides still win, and the sources say so).

BluetoothState.description: GET /api/v1/audio/bluetooth/state: the adapter condition. available=false means the Bluetooth controller is not wired into this build (no system bus, no BlueZ daemon) - the page hides the section; powered=false is the adapter-off state the page says out loud with the remediation.

synthetic.description: True when the controller is the labelled-synthetic fake (GAME_NARRATOR_BT_FAKE): the ADR-0074 rule that a fake answer never reads as hardware.

discovering.description: The adapter's Discovering property: a scan is in progress (ours or another client's).

alias.description: The adapter's friendly name (the system name).

note.description: A controller-level finding the page surfaces verbatim (the powered-off remediation, the bluez-missing fact).

BluetoothDevice.description: One Bluetooth device row (ADR-0091). address is the stable identity - never the BlueZ object path, which is a per-boot allocation. The pairing flags are BlueZ's own Device1 properties (reported, never inferred); the A2DP flags are the UUID evidence. selected and needs_repair are the page's derivations: selected marks the device whose A2DP sink (bluez_output.<MAC>.1) the audio selection resolves to; needs_repair is issue #3's state - BlueZ reports the device connected (a GATT connection counts) yet no A2DP unit exists, the LE-only regression the repair route exists for.

alias.description: BlueZ's display name (the remote name when no alias is set); empty while the name has not resolved.

trusted.description: The Trusted property: trusted devices connect without further confirmation.

connected.description: BlueZ's Connected property. A GATT-only connection counts - which is exactly why needs_repair exists.

a2dp_sink.description: The device advertises the A2DP service: it can receive the narration audio (the audio-capable filter).

a2dp_source.description: The device advertises the A2DP Source (the reverse direction); reported for the "why is this not a sink" question.

rssi.description: The last measured signal strength, when BlueZ reports it.

discovered.description: Seen in the most recent scan (whether or not paired): a scan that finds only unpaired devices is the "put the headset in pairing mode" evidence.

selected.description: True when the effective audio selection resolves to this device's A2DP sink (bluez_output.<MAC>.1).

needs_repair.description: The issue-#3 state: connected and paired yet no A2DP unit. The page offers the re-pair (repair) button.

BluetoothDevices.description: GET /api/v1/audio/bluetooth/devices and the scan inventory: every device BlueZ has a record of (paired or merely discovered), with the pairing state, the A2DP evidence and the selection badge.

note.description: A scan-level finding (the pairing-mode hint when the scan finds nothing).

BluetoothScanRequest.description: POST /api/v1/audio/bluetooth/scan: the operator bound on how long to hold the discovery open. Absent, the 8 s default; below 1 s clamps to 1 s; above 30 s clamps to 30 s (a longer hold buys nothing - the pairing-mode headset answers in seconds).

duration_ms.description: The hold in milliseconds: absent = the 8 s default; below 1 clamps to 1; above 30000 clamps to 30000.

BluetoothScan.description: The scan answer: the inventory the scan left behind plus the timing the page progress state reports. An empty inventory is a 200 with the pairing-mode hint in note - a scan that finds nothing is an answer, not a failure.

elapsed_ms.description: How long the discovery actually held the inquiry channel.

BluetoothAction.description: The answer of every Bluetooth device mutation (pair, trust, connect, disconnect, forget, repair): the address the operation ran on (the row the page refetches) and the product-level result note.

address.description: The normalised (upper-case) MAC the operation ran on.

private_hosts_allowed.description: The count of allowlist entries; the entries themselves are operator network topology and stay server-side.

source.description: Where the numbers live: build constants, not environment, in this build.

SettingsUpdate.description: The /settings page's version-and-updates section. current is the running build; latest is what the check last determined (fresh or from the offline cache), null when it knows no release (disabled, never ran, or failed with no cache); available is true only when latest is strictly newer than current and both parsed — a dev build never claims an update exists.

current.description: This build's version stamp (the current of current-vs-latest).

available.description: True when latest is strictly newer than current and both parsed.

checked_at.description: When latest was determined; absent when unknown.

from_cache.description: The offline-cache fallback: the fresh check failed and this is the last good answer.

checking.description: True while no check has completed yet (the first one runs at boot in the background).

no_releases.description: The endpoint answered and has no releases yet.

disabled.description: The operator turned the check off.

error.description: Set when the fresh check failed (with or without a cached answer): one line, no credentials.

env.description: The variables that control the check.

RestoreScheduled.description: The 202 answer of POST /api/v1/admin/restore (ADR-0090): the plan is durable on disk and the appliance is about to restart. The fields are what the operator reviews before the restart — the backup's identity (hash, size, schema version) and the pre-restore safety net's name.

RestorePlan.description: The restore plan's operator-facing projection (base names only: absolute paths are host state and stay server-side, docs/spec/08).

RestoreStatus.description: The GET /api/v1/admin/restore answer (ADR-0090): what the last restore did (or that one is pending). The UI polls this after the restart.

count.description: 0 in this build: nothing is runtime-mutable.

env.description: The variables that control the rendered values.

Settings.description: The effective configuration of the running process, read-only where it comes from the environment (docs/spec/09 /settings). Secrets never reach the browser: tokens are presence booleans, endpoints are '<configured>'.

ScenarioView.description: One row of the scenario catalog (a testdata/scenarios YAML as the loader parsed it).

GateView.description: One gate's latest recorded result from artifacts/gates.

instruction.description: What makes the gate run (the make target plus its prerequisites) — the actionable form of NOT RUN.

DolphinReadiness.description: The Arch-side Dolphin prerequisites, by presence only: booleans and variable names, never paths (docs/spec/14).

ProviderReadiness.description: Which model roles this process has configured, by name only.

DevTests.description: The /tests page's snapshot: the scenario catalog, the recorded gate results, and the Dolphin/provider readiness of this host.

repo_root_known.description: false: no repository root could be resolved; the catalog and gates are empty by design.

ScenarioRunStatus.description: The run job's state plus, once succeeded, the report's links.

state.description: queued, running, succeeded, failed, cancelled or recoverable.

status.description: passed, failed or blocked, once the job is terminal.

report.description: Route paths to the stored report blobs.

CorrectionKind.description: What kind of mistake the correction fixed.

CorrectionStatus.description: The review state. A correction is a proposal until a reviewer accepts it; the editor's own save is accepted by the acting curator in the same request (ADR-0052).

Correction.description: One correction label — the regression fixture of its target: what was wrong (before_value), what it should be (after_value, the assertion a re-run checks) and who decided (actor). A correction of a message's speech text is recorded by the dialogue editor's save itself; explicit recordings land as proposed (ADR-0052).

target_id.description: Loose pointer to the corrected row; the label outlives the row (0002).

message_id.description: Set when the target is a message, so the common lookup is an index seek.

before_value.description: What was wrong before the fix.

after_value.description: What it should be — the assertion a re-run checks. Required for an accepted correction; may be absent on a proposal the reviewer has not settled.

actor.description: Who made the correction (username, or agent:<run id>).

reviewer.description: Present once the correction is accepted or rejected.

reviewed_at.description: Present once the correction is accepted or rejected.

CorrectionList.description: Correction labels, newest first (created_at, then id). The developer's fixture browsing surface (GET /api/v1/dev/fixtures) serves the same rows: a correction is the regression fixture of its target (ADR-0052).

CreateCorrectionRequest.description: Record a correction explicitly — the inspector's "text incorrect / speaker incorrect" actions. This records a label only; it never applies a fix. The row lands as proposed with the caller as actor (ADR-0052).

target_id.description: Required. The row the correction is about.

message_id.description: For a message target: must equal target_id when present.

after_value.description: What it should be; the proposal's asserted fix.

name.description: The basename the request sends; never a path.

DiscImages.description: GET /api/v1/import/disc/images: what the allowlisted directory holds, without naming the directory.

configured.description: true when the operator has configured the import directory; a 200 with false and an empty list is the unconfigured answer.

adapter.description: id@semver of the disc-capable adapter linked into this build, when one is.

DiscImportRequest.description: The dir shape's body. The image is a basename directly in the allowlisted import directory; anything path-shaped is a 400.

DiscImportAccepted.description: The image is verified and the import queued; progress and the report are the job's.

source.description: Which shape the job will read: the allowlisted file in place, or the upload's content from the asset store.

sha256.description: The image's content hash, upload shape only (the dir shape hashes in the job and reports it in its result).

allOf.description: The result_json of a succeeded import.disc job: the file-import counters the review screen reads, plus the disc-side provenance (the image's own hash, the disc's game id and region).

image_sha256.description: The disc image's SHA-256 — provenance in place of the path, which is never stored (AGENTS.md rule 5/6).

game_id.description: The disc boot header's game id, e.g. GZLE01.

disc_region.description: The region the game id maps to; the edition's region is the curator's choice and a mismatch is the review's business.

Clip.description: A replay clip installed under the managed clip store (ADR-0073): the id a session selects by, the install-time summary, and the archive's provenance. No host path appears in this object.

id.description: The clip id: a lowercase slug a session's frame_source.clip_id selects by, and the store's directory name.

name.description: The display name the upload carried; absent when the id came from the archive.

frames.description: The frame count the import validated from the clip's timestamps.json manifest.

archive_sha256.description: The content hash of the uploaded archive, committed to the asset store: the clip's provenance is verifiable against the store.

archive_size.description: The uploaded archive's size in bytes.

archive_format.description: The container the upload arrived in; unknown for a clip the store adopted from a directory it found without a provenance row.

created_by.description: The account that installed the clip; recovered when the store adopted a directory without a provenance row.

missing.description: True when the index has the clip but its directory is gone: it cannot start a session, and the delete is a cleanup.

ClipUploaded.description: The 201 answer to a clip upload: the installed clip's record plus the detail sentence.

id.description: The clip id: a lowercase slug a session's frame_source.clip_id selects by, and the store's directory name.

name.description: The display name the upload carried; absent when the id came from the archive.

frames.description: The frame count the import validated from the clip's timestamps.json manifest.

archive_sha256.description: The content hash of the uploaded archive, committed to the asset store: the clip's provenance is verifiable against the store.

archive_size.description: The uploaded archive's size in bytes.

archive_format.description: The container the upload arrived in (the list's Clip additionally admits unknown for a clip the store adopted from a directory without a provenance row).

created_by.description: The account that installed the clip; recovered when the store adopted a directory without a provenance row.

missing.description: True when the index has the clip but its directory is gone: it cannot start a session, and the delete is a cleanup.

detail.description: What the upload did and how to use the result: the asset store's hash and the frame_source a session starts with.

ClipList.description: The managed clip store as listed: one record per installed clip, index order.

CaptureLink.description: The device's USB link (internal/capture/usb): the negotiated speed, its class, and the ADR-0076 downgrade flag (a SuperSpeed-class port that negotiated USB 2 — the 're-seat' fault).

speed_mbps.description: The negotiated link speed in Mb/s (480 = HighSpeed/USB 2, 5000 = SuperSpeed).

downgraded.description: True when a faster port negotiated a slower link: re-seat the dongle or try another port (the ADR-0076 fault).

CaptureMode.description: A capture mode: the geometry, the frame rate and the pixel format the device offers and the session asks for.

CaptureChosen.description: The mode the session will ask for on the device: the operator's pinned mode when it is still offered (source 'saved'), otherwise the ADR-0076 policy's pick (source 'policy') with the policy's reason and rejected-candidate count, so 'why 720p and not 1080p' stays answerable.

source.description: Who decided the mode: the operator's pin or the ADR-0076 policy.

reason.description: The policy reason (the pin names no reason; the policy explains the pick).

rejected.description: How many offered candidates the policy rejected before this pick.

CaptureDevice.description: One enumerated capture node: its stable id, the USB link, the state and the chosen mode.

id.description: The device's stable id (the udev by-id name, the by-path name, or the node path): the only name a session or a selection may use.

name.description: The card name the enumeration printed.

path.description: The node path (report only — a client never names a path, the enumeration is the allowlist).

state.description: ready: a mode fits; no-formats: the node enumerates none; no-mode: none fit the policy; enumeration-error: the format read failed (detail carries the fault); not-capture: a non-capture node.

detail.description: The operator action for a non-ready state (the policy refusal, the enumeration fault).

CaptureDevices.description: GET /api/v1/capture/devices: the enumeration, the current selection and the synthetic flag.

synthetic.description: True when the list is the labelled test seam (GAME_NARRATOR_CAPTURE_FAKE): the UI says so, and no answer is mistaken for hardware.

note.description: The one-line provenance a synthetic list reports.

selected_id.description: The persisted selection (the device a session without an explicit id runs); absent when the operator never chose one.

CaptureSelectionRequest.description: PUT /api/v1/capture/devices/{id} body: the optional pinned mode. Omitting it records 'the policy decides for this device'.

CaptureSelection.description: The saved capture selection: the device and, when pinned, the mode.

CaptureBox.description: A pixel region of the current frame (the probe OCR region, the user-selected box of docs/spec/10).

CaptureProbeRequest.description: POST /api/v1/capture/probe body: the device (empty = the stack resolution), the frame count (0 = default 20, capped 200) and the OCR region (absent = the centre third).

CaptureProbeOCR.description: The probe's OCR block: the text read from the region, the box read, and the engine (or 'unavailable' with the install action when the engine is not wired — the degradable half).

note.description: The operator action when the engine did not run.

CaptureProbe.description: POST /api/v1/capture/probe: the docs/spec/10 capture test — the frame stats (freshness and drops) and the OCR block.

device.description: The stable id of the device the probe ran on.

mode.description: The mode asked of the device (e.g. "640x480 MJPEG @ 10 fps").

dropped.description: Frames dropped (slot overwrites) across the grab: the dropped-frame check.

freshness_ms.description: Milliseconds since the last frame: the freshness check.

state.description: The source state at the end of the grab.

last_error.description: The source last failure text (the operator action).

SettingsUpdateLatest.description: The release the update check last determined (fresh or from the offline cache).

HostCPU.description: The CPU facts of the host section (ADR-0087). Load averages and the throttle counters are null when the kernel does not expose them (non-Linux, or the sysfs file is absent): null is the honest state, never a zero that reads as measured.

load_1m.description: The 1-minute load average (/proc/loadavg); null when unreadable.

load_5m.description: The 5-minute load average; null when unreadable.

load_15m.description: The 15-minute load average; null when unreadable.

throttle_count.description: The summed x86 CPU thermal-throttle counters (/sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu*/thermal_throttle/throttle_count); null where the kernel does not expose the file (ARM).

HostRAM.description: The RAM facts from /proc/meminfo; the whole object is null when the kernel does not expose it.

HostStorage.description: The storage facts of the host section. data_dir is the data directory's base name only (the absolute path is a host path and stays server-side, the settingsStorage rule); the byte counts are -1 when the filesystem could not be measured.

data_dir.description: The data directory's base name; empty when unknown.

free_bytes.description: Free space on the data directory's filesystem; -1 when unmeasured.

total_bytes.description: Total size of the data directory's filesystem; -1 when unmeasured.

asset_store_bytes.description: The asset store's byte total; -1 when unmeasured.

ThermalZone.description: One thermal zone read from /sys/class/thermal (ADR-0087: from sysfs where present).

name.description: The zone's type file content (e.g. cpu-thermal).

celsius.description: The zone's temperature in Celsius (the temp file's millidegrees / 1000).

HostThermal.description: The thermal state of the host. available is true only when at least one zone read; with no zones the note says so, because an empty list must not read as all cool.

note.description: The unavailable state's reason (absent when available).

HostReport.description: The GET /api/v1/diagnostics/host body: a system-info-class read (docs/spec/08) — host capacity and state, no game content, no host paths beyond the data directory's base name, no secrets. The warnings derive from fixed thresholds (1 GiB free, load above cores, 85 °C, 10% RAM) so the operator can verify each against the same section.

warnings.description: The derived warnings; empty when nothing crossed a threshold.

DiagnosticsRunRequest.description: The POST /api/v1/diagnostics/run body (ADR-0087): zero to seven of docs/spec/06's role names; empty asks for the host snapshot only. The enumeration is the allowlist — a name that is not one of the seven is a 400.

DiagnosticsRunRef.description: The 202 answer of POST /api/v1/diagnostics/run: the id to poll on GET /api/v1/diagnostics/{id}.

DiagnosticsRole.description: One role's doctor answer in a diagnostics run: the doctor's status (the same vocabulary the CLI's report uses), its summary and remedy, and the probe's measured duration — the latency, as the measured number, never an estimate.

configured.description: Whether the role has a model configured (the settings page's fact).

status.description: The doctor's state for the role's probe.

detail.description: The probe's evidence; redacted (the doctor's safeText, never a token).

remedy.description: The operator action for a non-OK row.

duration_ms.description: The probe's measured wall-clock duration in milliseconds.

DiagnosticsRun.description: The GET /api/v1/diagnostics/{id} body: the run's current shape. A running run reports the host snapshot and the role rows answered so far, so the page polls one shape; done adds finished_at. 404 (problem) for an id never created or already evicted from the bounded store (32 runs, one-hour TTL after done).

roles.description: The role rows answered so far; empty while none has landed.

requested.description: The role names the run was asked for.

finished_at.description: Set when the run is done.

LogRecord.description: One record of the process's log tail. Every message and attribute value has passed the support-bundle redactor (ADR-0042's scrubber: URLs, tokens and private IPs replaced) before it left the process (AGENTS.md rule 5).

level.description: The slog level name (INFO, WARN, ERROR, …).

attrs.description: The record's attributes, values rendered to strings and redacted.

DiagnosticsLogs.description: The GET /api/v1/diagnostics/logs body: the newest records of the process's bounded log ring (developer tier, like the dev-trace evidence route — system logs can carry provider request detail). The tail is process-local: a restart clears it, and the durable redacted path is the support bundle.

DevFixtureEntry.description: One file of a recorded fixture: its path inside the fixture directory, the content's SHA-256 and its size (ADR-0054's manifest shape; a manifest cannot carry its own hash).

DevFixture.description: A recorded trace fixture's identity and where it landed (ADR-0083), so the operator sees exactly where the evidence left the machine. dir is the external fixture root's entry, named (never an absolute host path the UI should act on).

DevFixtureRecordRequest.description: The fixture recording's body: the trace whose observation, expectation, audio and labels become one replayable unit.

DevFixtureRecordResponse.description: The 201 body of POST /api/v1/dev/fixtures: the fixture's identity and where it landed.

DevRerunCandidate.description: One re-ranked message: the same decomposition the recorded candidates carry (score, probability, components) so the diff the page renders compares like with like.

DevRerunRanking.description: One side of the re-run: the candidate table, the winner's margin, the matcher's reason code and the abstain flag.

DevRerunDiffRow.description: One candidate's movement between the two rankings: a null rank or probability is the candidate's absence on that side.

DevRerunDecision.description: The re-run's honesty note (ADR-0083 decision 3): whether the recorded trace involved a provider adjudication, and that this route recomputes the local decision path only — the model is not re-invoked, because the session's decision wiring is fenced per session.

DevRerunResponse.description: The 200 body of the re-run: the stored observation it re-ran, the recorded ranking, the re-ranked one, the diff and the decision note.

Status.description: One snapshot of what the box is doing (docs/design/plum-peach Global chrome). status is the canonical short string the status bar renders, produced by the server (RenderStatus) so every client shows the same text; the structured halves below are what the string is rendered from.

status.description: The canonical status string, e.g. '● live · capture 30fps · 412ms frame→voice', '● agent running · 9 of 12 voiced · 18m 04s' or '5 ok · 1 slow'. A live session's string appends the non-ok health tiles; the idle string is the health rollup.

session.description: The active narration session; absent when the box is not narrating.

setup_runs.description: The active onboarding runs, newest first (usually zero or one); absent when none is live.

StatusSession.description: The active session's bar view: the game, the mode, the capture rate actual against target, the dropped frames, the frame-to-voice p50 the session samples per line (the pipeline's frame-to-committed half plus the last-N commit-to-voice half), and the lines the box actually spoke.

game.description: The game's title; absent while the store cannot name it (unwired store or a profile with no game row).

source.description: The frame source kind (v4l2, replay, dolphin, test_pattern, manual).

capture_fps.description: The source's measured rate; 0 while it has not delivered frames.

capture_fps_target.description: The rate the session asked of its device; absent for source kinds with no named rate.

lines_spoken.description: Playbacks the sink started: the lines actually voiced, not the lines committed.

frame_to_voice_p50_ms.description: The bar's latency number in whole milliseconds: the pipeline's frame-to-committed p50 (whole-run, per-line samples) plus the session's commit-to-voice p50 (last-N window), each half contributing when it has samples; 0 while no half does.

frame_to_voice_samples.description: Lines that went into the commit-to-voice half; 0 means the number is the frame-to-committed half alone.

StatusSetupRun.description: One active onboarding run's bar view: the state, the step the agent is on (stage), the characters voiced against the total, and the run's age.

game.description: The run's game title: the profile's game once the run has a profile, the plan's title before that; absent when neither names one.

state.description: The live run states (docs/spec/03); terminal runs are not status data.

stage.description: The newest tool call's name: the step the agent is on; absent before the first tool call.

voiced.description: Characters with a non-retired voice revision.

StatusHealth.description: The six-tile rollup (capture, ocr, decision, tts, agent, storage) in canonical order, with the counts the bar renders as '5 ok · 1 slow'.

unknown.description: Components nobody has probed; the rollup says so rather than counting them ok.

detail.description: The rendered rollup, the idle bar's whole string.

StatusHealthComponent.description: One health tile: the component's level and its one-line detail (the evidence, or the fact that there is none).

level.description: unknown is a component nobody has probed (or is not active), which is not ok: a rollup that counted it ok would lie.

StatusDevice.description: The box itself: the build, how long it has run, and the bound listen address when one was wired.

listen_addr.description: The bound listen address (the tailnet address when the host bound the tailnet); absent when the host did not wire it.

AssistantScreenContext.description: The dock's current screen (UX-01). Every field optional; a message without context is still a valid turn. Bounded and validated at the write edge: the route is a path-only string, the ids are ULIDs, visible_ids is at most 64 entries.

game_id.description: The game the screen shows, when it names one.

profile_id.description: The profile revision the screen shows, when it names one.

type.description: The selection kind, e.g. character or line.

visible_ids.description: The ids visible on the screen (roster order, timeline order).

thread_id.description: An existing thread of the caller; absent or empty opens a new thread.

AssistantMessageAccepted.description: The turn is stored and the attempt queued; the reply streams over the event hub (assistant.message, assistant.question, the loop's step and tool events).

run_id.description: The durable agent run the thread owns.

job_id.description: The assistant.run attempt that will handle the turn.

answer.description: The operator's answer; for a confirmation card it is confirm or cancel (an empty answer defers the question).

AssistantAnswerAccepted.description: The answer is durable (a user message in the conversation plus the question row's answered state). Exactly one follow-up attempt is owed: enqueued here when no attempt is in flight (job_id present), otherwise owned by the in-flight attempt's post-run hook (job_id absent).

job_id.description: The follow-up attempt, when this call queued one.

state.description: The run's state (queued, running, blocked, review, failed, succeeded, cancelled) or unknown.

next_cursor.description: Empty when this is the last page.

AssistantToolCardView.description: One executed tool call the dock renders as a compact card (name, result, duration, state).

state.description: The wrapped result's status (succeeded, failed, refused, timeout, cancelled) or the row's own state while pending.

result_preview.description: A bounded preview of the structured result.

AssistantQuestionView.description: One NEEDS-YOU card: the model's question or a mutating tool's confirmation (UX-04). Unanswered cards carry no answer field.

AssistantThreadSnapshot.description: The REST snapshot a page that missed the stream rebuilds from: the conversation tail, the open and recent questions, and the tool cards.

CloneRequest.description: The optional body of the clone. Absent or empty takes the ADR-0107 defaults: the source game's title, and the source slug suffixed -copy, then -2, -3, ... until the slug is free.

CloneLink.description: One provenance row of clone_links (ADR-0107): where a clone came from. Immutable; the table is queryable in both directions (source profile, target game).

CloneResponse.description: The clone's 201 body: the four rows the one store transaction created (ADR-0107).

PurgeReport.description: The purge's 200 body (ADR-0107): what the transaction removed and the blobs its post-commit reference-before-delete pass dropped.

SetupBoardCharacter.description: One card of the setup board snapshot.

stage.description: The card column the character is in (UX-06).

at.description: The observed time of the character newest setup.character_stage event; absent when the event log holds none.

SetupRailCell.description: One cell of the setup page six-cell stage rail (plan.md item 4).

value.description: The cell number (line count, character counts, the profile status on the publish cell).

SetupProgress.description: The run-level state behind the setup page tiles and rail; also the setup.progress SSE payload (ADR-0108).

lines_read.description: The profile total dialogue line count.

voiced.description: Characters at stage voicing or later (a TTS take exists; done means it is approved).

elapsed.description: Whole seconds since the run was created.

SetupBoard.description: The setup board snapshot (ADR-0108, UX-06): the page load that cannot trust the stream rebuilds the board from this body. Every field is derived from the same durable rows the setup.* events carry.
